# What a Repository Is

#### Course: Practical Git and GitHub

## What a Repository Is

If Git lets you save your progress, then the next question is simple.

Where are those saves kept?

In Git, everything lives inside something called a repository.

A repository is just your project, but with memory. It keeps track of every version you save, so nothing is lost as you continue working.

![A folder icon with a small .git subfolder visible inside it](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

You don't need multiple copies of your project or confusing file names. You work in one place, and Git keeps a clear history of everything behind the scenes.

👉 Next, let's see why this makes such a big difference in real projects.
